about: PD-49 game mechanics (plan section C). Each is signed once by a teacher and the scholar (scope 'play' in the review system) before any child plays it; until then it never appears. A mechanic's record is what is signed, and it carries the SHA-256 of its game's code plus the shared play code (everything that changes what a game does: the card, the knobs, the session, the page and its route, the registry, the shuffle, the recitation and the verified-text loader; check-quran-content.py SHARED_CODE): change the record or the code and it waits for review again. The respect rules are the plan's section C.4, stated for this mechanic.

respect: Each ayah is shown whole, still and unaltered, as the verified text gives it.
Only the card's frame glows while that ayah is recited; the text never moves, shrinks, bounces or changes.
The child taps the card to hear the ayah again; nothing is popped, thrown, caught or hidden.
No music and no instruments: the recitation itself is the only sound.
One ayah at a time, shown whole and unaltered while it is recited.
After the recitation the child repeats aloud; nothing is recorded or stored, and a grown-up taps to say it was repeated.
No music and no instruments; no score for the child's voice.
Every card is a whole, real ayah of the verified text; no card is ever an altered or made-up ayah.
A wrong tap is refused where it is: the card stays as it is, and after two tries the right ayah is shown and praised.
Each card has a shape and a number as well as a colour, so it is never told apart by colour alone.
No timer, no lost points, no music.
The segment's ayat are shown whole and in order; the next one to count is lit by its frame only.
A grown-up reads each ayah to the child (or the recitation plays, where it is allowed), then the child touches it to count.
Nothing is moved, hidden or scored; no music.
The tiles are the words of one ayah of the verified text, each whole with its pause mark; no word from anywhere else is ever offered.
Words are tiles placed in a line, never objects to catch, stack, feed, throw or step on.
A tile out of turn is refused where it sits: the line only ever holds the ayah's own words in their order, and what is not yet built is shown as blanks, never as an ayah.
Once built, the whole verified ayah is shown as it is.
Only ayat of three to six words (6-8, which starts with the first word placed) or three to ten (9-12) are built; longer ayat are not cut.
No timer, no lost points, no music.
Every card is a whole, real ayah of the verified text; only whole ayat are reordered, and no ayah is ever changed.
A card's number is hidden until it is in place, so the order is found from the ayat themselves.

3-5: two neighbouring ayat, which comes first; after two tries the answer is shown and praised. 6-8 and 9-12: a card out of turn is refused where it sits, so the ordered list only ever holds ayat in their true order.
Two ayat with the same words are never asked to be told apart.
No timer, no lost points, no music.

Each half is a real ayah of the verified text cut at a word boundary, shown as a half: marked with an ellipsis where it was cut and named as the start or the end of an ayah, so it never reads as an ayah.
A start is never joined to an end that is not its own: a wrong end is refused where it sits, and nothing assembled from two ayat is ever shown.
A matched pair is shown as the whole verified ayah.
No two starts and no two ends have the same words, so every match has one answer.
No timer, no lost points, no music.
The ayah asked about and every choice are whole, real ayat of the same surah, from the verified text, shown as they are; a choice is never an altered or made-up ayah.
The choices carry no number until answered. Wrong choices have other words than the answer: for 6-8 never a neighbour, for 9-12 the nearest ayat; 9-12 is also asked which comes before.
A wrong choice is refused where it sits, and then the right ayah is shown.
No timer, no lost points, no music.
The ayah is the verified text with one word hidden (two for 9-12), and each hidden word is shown as a blank, never as a guess; its pause mark stays in its place.
The choices are real words of the same surah, shown as words; none looks like the answer with other marks.
A wrong choice is refused where it is and never put into the blank, so no false ayah is ever on screen; a right one fills the blank with the ayah's own word.
Once complete, the whole verified ayah is shown.
No timer, no lost points, no music.
The ayah is shown whole first; at each step more of its words are hidden, never changed, moved or replaced.
For 9-12 a hidden word leaves only its first letter, in a box and named as a cue, never as the word or as an ayah; the last step is first letters only.
The child recites aloud and can touch a hidden word to see it again; nothing is recorded, scored or stored.
At the end the whole verified ayah is shown.
No timer, no music.
Every ayah shown is a whole, real ayah of the verified text, without its number until answered.
An ayah whose words appear again in the surah is never asked, so every question has one answer.
A wrong choice is refused; then the answer is shown, with the numbers.
No timer, no lost points, no music.
